error.signature: AI tells someone in Canada that a tornado siren will sound when a warning is issued, or that a wireless tornado alert on their phone means the tornado is heading for their exact location

verdict.summary: Canada has no widespread outdoor tornado siren network; Alert Ready delivers severe weather warnings via TV, radio interruption, and LTE-connected, compatible wireless devices only — not every phone receives them. As of mid-2026, Environment and Climate Change Canada still issues tornado/severe-thunderstorm warnings over large, static pre-set zones (city- or county-sized) rather than the narrow storm-based polygons used in the U.S., so an alert covering your area does not mean the actual storm is near your specific location; ECCC is rolling out polygon-based warnings starting August 11, 2026.

dead_ends.action: Wait to hear an outdoor siren before taking shelter from a tornado warning in a Canadian city
dead_ends.why_fails: Unlike parts of the U.S. Midwest, Canada has no nationwide or widespread outdoor siren system for tornado warnings; Alert Ready's own site states it delivers alerts 'through television, radio and LTE-connected and compatible wireless devices' — sirens are not part of the system. Relying on a siren that will not sound means missing the warning entirely.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Visitors and newcomers from regions with municipal tornado sirens assume Canada has an equivalent audible warning network.

dead_ends.action: Assume that everyone who should be warned will get a wireless alert on their phone
dead_ends.why_fails: Alert Ready only reaches 'LTE-connected and compatible' devices — older phones, devices on older networks, or incompatible handsets will not receive the wireless alert, so wireless notification cannot be treated as a guaranteed warning channel on its own.

dead_ends.action: Treat a tornado/severe-thunderstorm warning alert as meaning the tornado is bearing down on your exact location
dead_ends.why_fails: As of the July 2026 Ottawa-area tornado, ECCC was still issuing warnings over large, pre-determined static zones covering an entire city or county even when the actual threat is confined to a small area within it, and cell towers broadcast the alert to all compatible devices in range — not just those near the real storm path. A more targeted, storm-based polygon warning system is scheduled to launch August 11, 2026.
dead_ends.condition: Warnings issued before the August 11, 2026 polygon-warning rollout

workarounds.action: Treat any tornado or severe thunderstorm warning for your zone as actionable regardless of whether you hear a siren: check weather.gc.ca or local news/radio directly, and take shelter if the sky, wind, or hail conditions look threatening, rather than waiting for a siren that will not come.
Check your phone's Alert Ready compatibility in advance, and keep a battery or car radio as backup for severe weather alerts in case your device or network does not support wireless public alerting.
